title: Broadcasting, axes and mutation order
outcome: Use broadcasting with explicit axes and distinguish an elementwise formula from a mutation-order-dependent algorithm.

exercises.title: Choose the axis
exercises.task: Add one offset per column to a matrix.
exercises.expected: Reshape the offsets into a one-row array.
exercises.answer: The explicit singleton axis documents the intended broadcast alignment.

exercises.title: Reject incompatible axes
exercises.task: Broadcast a length 4 vector with the 2-by -3 fixture.
exercises.hint: Compatible axes are not determined by total element count.
exercises.answer: Shape validation prevents a silent interpretation of an unintended operation.

exercises.title: Update in place
exercises.task: Apply 2x+1 elementwise to a floating vector using dotted assignment.
exercises.expected: The destination values change to the expected affine result.
exercises.hint: Each output depends only on the corresponding old element.
exercises.answer: This dependence pattern makes the specific self-update straightforward to reason about.

exercises.title: Trace a manual recurrence
exercises.task: Shift a vector left-to-right by reading the preceding updated element.
exercises.hint: A later read sees an earlier write.
exercises.answer: The loop implements a recurrence, not a simultaneous snapshot assignment.

exercises.title: Preserve a snapshot
exercises.task: Read the shift input from an explicit copy.
exercises.answer: The copy changes the read/write dependency and therefore the algorithm.

exercises.title: Choose a destination type
exercises.task: Write 0.5 into an integer element through dotted assignment.
exercises.hint: Mutation does not make the destination representation arbitrary.
exercises.answer: Allocate a representation that can express the intended result.
